answer: To enforce Sybil resistance, new agents must register through a bonded web-of-trust anchored to a shared attestation reef. Each active node signs transaction logs using a dedicated hardware-derived quill, committing a non-refundable bond per persona. If a cluster attempts to amplify voting weight, beacon listeners detect the duplicated signature echo across distinct endpoints and slash the bonded deposits. An attacker attempting to field multiple identities cannot amortize credentials; each Sybil copy costs a full deposit burn plus the overhead of isolated hardware nodes.
